title: FTSE Russell Q1 2027 quarterly review takes effect at the open — IPO adds, quarterly shares-in-issue and free-float updates, and the Russell US Style capping recap all implement after the 2027-03-19 quad-witching close
source: EST: owner-published standing rule, re-derived and re-verified first-hand this session rather than inherited from the proposal. FTSE Russell, "Frequently Asked Questions — Russell US Equity Indexes", July 2026 (lseg.com dam policy-documents, ftse-faq-document-russell-us-equity-2026.pdf, HTTP 200, 198,134 bytes, 19 content streams inflated and text-extracted in-session 2026-09-09 to 17,354 printable characters — byte and stream counts reproduce what three sibling ledgers recorded, which is the check that this is the same edition). Two of its tables give the date. The "Quarterly Addition Guidelines" table publishes the STANDING RULE, not one year's dates: Rank Date "Last working day in January and July", Announce Date "Fourth Friday prior to the effective date (after market close)", Effective Date "Third Friday of the month", footnoted "** After the close on the third Friday of the month" and "* If a date falls on a holiday the previous business day is used". The dated four-column schedule table publishes "Review Effective Date (open of) — 23 March 2026 / 29 June 2026 / 21 September 2026 / 14 December 2026" against "Russell US Style Capping Cut-Off Date — 11 March 2026 / 17 June 2026 / 9 September 2026 / 2 December 2026" and "Lock-Down Period (open of) — 9 March 2026 / 8 June 2026 / 7 September 2026 / 30 November 2026". The rule reproduces both published QUARTERLY columns to the day (third Fridays 20 March and 18 September 2026 → effective opens 23 March and 21 September 2026), and the capping cut-off is the same twelve calendar days before the effective Monday in all four published columns. The third Friday of March 2027 is 2027-03-19 — already tracked here as opex-2027-03-19 — so the review implements after that close and is effective at the open of Monday 2027-03-22, with the style capping cut-off Wednesday 2027-03-10, lock-down opening Monday 2027-03-08, announce Friday 2027-02-19 and rank date Friday 2027-01-29. The 2027 dates are RULE-DERIVED, NOT PUBLISHED: the FAQ's dated table carries 2026 columns only, the string "2027" appears nowhere in the document, and it closes "NOTE: Dates may be subject to change. Clients will be notified of any changes." The already-tracked russell-quarterly-ipo-review-effective-2026-09-21 is the owner's other instance of the same review under the same rule, so this is the missing 2027 member of a series this calendar already carries rather than a new class. Stays estimate because the confirmed-tier prefixes in market-events-data.ts have no member for an index owner's own schedule, because the 2027 dates are derived rather than published, and because this lane does not self-confirm. Canonical file written 2026-09-09 by this event's initial research, after reading the one proposal that carried this id (proposals/russell-quarterly-ipo-review-effective-2027-03-22.from-russell-style-quarter-end-capping-effective-2027-03-31.json)
notes:
SCOPE IS WIDER THAN THE 2026-09-21 SIBLING RECORDED, from the owner's own words. That ledger's signal list states "Scope is small by construction — IPO adds only, from the 1 May-31 July 2026 window; no cap-tier migration, no style re-scoring, no float re-weighting." The FAQ's Index Maintenance section, read verbatim this session, says otherwise for the March leg: "March 2026 — The cut-off date for quarterly shares in issue and free float changes will be the last business day in January", and its December note calls the 3% buffer the one "typically used at quarterly reviews". So a quarterly review implements THREE things, not one: the IPO additions from the 1 November-29 January window, buffered shares-in-issue and free-float updates across existing constituents, and the Russell US Style capping recap struck at the 2027-03-10 cut-off. The correction does not change the call — this ledger measures the same index-level null the sibling did, on more evidence — but it removes the sibling's stated REASON for the null, which matters to anyone later tempted to size the mechanism from that sentence.

THE CORRIDOR IS STRUCTURAL, NOT A 2026 ACCIDENT. Because the effective open is always the Monday after the third Friday, every instance of this event in either leg lands on the first session after a quarterly quad-witching expiry — rule-certain, no sampling involved. The FOMC adjacency is nearly as tight: on federalreserve.gov's own calendar (fetched direct 2026-09-09) the March FOMC decision falls within one week of the review effective Monday in all seven years the page carries (2021-2027), and 2027's is 16-17 March, two sessions before this open. This calendar independently tracks fomc-2027-03-17 (high), boj-decision-2027-03-18 and opex-2027-03-19 (high) inside the corridor, plus jpx-market-closure-2027-03-22 on the day itself. The 2026-09-21 sibling treated this contamination as a property of its own draw ("the 2026 print will be near-worthless as evidence"); it is a property of the class.

DOUBLE INDEX-FLOW OPEN: sp-quarterly-rebalance-effective-2027-03-22 is proposed for the same session by the same proposer. Impact low and symbols empty for the family's measured reasons — no house playbook is index-flow-keyed (re-grepped 2026-09-09, zero hits across trade-playbooks.md and multi-symbol-sweep.md), and an ETF proxy in symbols would make the deterministic screen trip on beta rather than on anything about this event.
